title.zh: 通用释放复核，感知终态（候选 v2）

description: Version 2 of the generic release review: the same question, frames and per-opening validity as version 1, but the episode is judged by what it ends on. It succeeds when at least `min_valid` openings are valid, the gripper does not close again after the last valid opening, and the last `place` time segment the live service committed for the episode (the one that starts last) is neither a failure nor unknown; no `place` segment fails it, an unknown one makes the verdict undecided (recorded as a failure). The place condition needs the time segments and is applied by the live service, not by the review run. General, not limited to tasks that place once: the gripper rule only looks after the LAST valid opening, so a task that grasps again between placements (stacking several plates, putting several screws in a box) is not failed by it. KNOWN LIMITS: (1) a false success is the larger risk: the rule counts neither how many placements happened nor which object, so it cannot stop an episode that stops half way or one that places the same object twice; `min_valid` (default 1) can set a task-level lower bound on valid openings. (2) a false failure happens when the review misses the last real placement (the last valid opening falls back to an earlier one, which is always followed by a close), or when the policy closes the gripper again after the final placement. CANDIDATE, NOT THE DEFAULT: checked offline on 91 eggplant-into-plate episodes (no false success in 61 failures, 30 of 30 successes kept), plus stacking plates (14 episodes) and putting two screws in a box (11 episodes) for false failures (0 of 39 real successes, 95 % upper bound about 0.09); the stacking plates and screws sets are small, hand-picked and partly not blind, so this is directional evidence, not a measured accuracy. Written 2026-10-04, wording corrected the same day; the rule is unchanged. Version 1 stays the default (`pipeline.anchored_spec`). The live page shows its verdict as automatic and unreviewed.
question:
A robot arm with a two-finger gripper is carrying out this instruction: "{task}". Work out what the instruction asks the robot to pick up and where it should end up.
The gripper receives an OPEN command at t=0; this is one release of the episode. Images 1-7 are the side camera at t=-2.5, -1.5, -0.8, -0.3, -0.1, +0.4, +1.2 s; images 8-11 are the wrist camera (looking down between the fingers) at t=-1.5, -0.6, -0.1, +0.4 s.
The gripper holds an object by pinching it, so a held object may hang tilted under the fingers; it counts as held if the whole object is off the surface it lay on and moves together with the gripper across the earlier images. An object that stays on the surface while the fingers close or drag it is NOT held.
Answer strictly from what the images show, not from what the robot seems to be trying to do:
- held_before: just before the open, is an object held off the surface by the fingers?
- landed: after the open, where is that object relative to what the instruction asks for: at_target if it rests on or in the place the instruction names as its destination; elsewhere if it rests somewhere else (the table, another object, a wrong container); still_in_gripper; nothing_released if no object was held.
- stays: at t=+1.2 s does it stay where it landed (not sliding, rolling or falling off)?
Use unclear whenever the images do not show it.
